primary_question: After repairing historical training adequacy, does temporal degradation persist in Future F1-F6?

scientific_conclusions.primary_question: After repairing historical training adequacy, does temporal degradation persist in Future F1-F6?
scientific_conclusions.conclusion_1_historical_training_repair: The optimized historical model substantially improves Future performance relative to the Day16 historical baseline across all six Future windows.
scientific_conclusions.conclusion_2_aggregate_temporal_generali: Broad aggregate temporal degradation largely disappears after optimization. Future pooled performance is approximately comparable to or slightly above Historical Validation at the point-estimate level.
scientific_conclusions.conclusion_3_residual_f3_failure: A localized residual temporal degradation remains in F3: Macro-F1 is significantly lower than Historical Validation, although the corresponding accuracy contrast is not distinguishable from zero.
scientific_conclusions.conclusion_4_class_specific_mechanism: The F3 degradation is class-specific rather than global. Positive recall falls sharply, while negative recall significantly improves and neutral recall remains comparatively stable.
scientific_conclusions.conclusion_5_error_direction: Among F3 true-positive observations, the dominant misclassification route is positive-to-negative rather than positive-to-neutral.
scientific_conclusions.conclusion_6_f4_residual: F4 retains a smaller but statistically supported positive-recall degradation, while F5 and F6 do not show statistically supported positive-recall degradation.
scientific_conclusions.overall_interpretation: The Day16 temporal degradation signal was partly attributable to insufficient historical model optimization. After optimization, most aggregate degradation is repaired, but a localized class-specific distribution-shift vulnerability remains, concentrated most strongly in F3 positive sentiment.

interpretation_boundary.supported: Historical optimization repairs most aggregate Future degradation, while statistically supported localized class-specific degradation remains.
interpretation_boundary.not_yet_established: The causal source of the F3 positive-to-negative shift has not yet been identified. No claim is made here regarding whether the mechanism is lexical, topical, source-composition, event-driven, label-distribution, or semantic-regime shift.
